en.title: GTAVI: An exclusive deep dive into the video game of the decade
en.description: This story is taken from the autumn 2026 issue of Dazed, which is on sale internationally from September 10. Pre-order a copy of the magazine here.
en.fullContent:
This story is taken from the autumn 2026 issue of Dazed, which is on sale internationally from September 10. Pre-order a copy of the magazine here.

On the sweltering Leonida Keys, sweat slicks the skin of two lovers on the run as they toast new beginnings, watching the sun set over the water. A breeze blows through their hair, and you can almost feel the condensation dripping from the cold beer bottles in their hands; in the background, locals gather on the weatherbeaten dock, indifferent to the story unfolding between the outlaws. Elsewhere, a few miles north, tanned bodies of all shapes and sizes swarm the sand on Vice Beach. Further north still, locals are caked in mud, kicked up from the back of a dirt bike or spattered on a stars-and-stripes bikini. And as night falls back in Vice City, sweaty crowds surge to deafening hip-hop beats, spilling out from clubs on to the neon-lit streets.

It’s been 13 years since Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto V, one of the most acclaimed – and controversial – video games of all time. And it’s been roughly the same amount of time since work began on its sequel, Grand Theft Auto VI, which transports the action from San Andreas (closely inspired by real-life southern California) to Leonida (based on Florida). That’s more than a decade of anticipation, meaning there’s “unprecedented pressure” on the follow-up to meet expectations, as Rob Nelson, head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, tells Dazed: “However, I don’t know that any amount of external pressure could compare with the pressure we put on ourselves as a team.”

If you accept that video games are an artform, then Rockstar Games has produced two of the most significant works of the 21st century so far: GTAV and the western-themed adventure Red Dead Redemption 2. The numbers speak for themselves: in 2013, the former broke the record for the fastest-selling entertainment product of all time, earning a billion dollars in just three days – more than any book or Hollywood film. Five years later, RDR2 took the second spot. But the latter also came with a gear shift. While GTA satirised modern life with wacky characters, high-octane car chases and explosive gunfights, RDR2 was hailed as one of the most realistic and immersive games to date, with a slower, more emotional tone suited to its storyline.

GTAVI promises something in between the two. The open-world game is set in the same fictionalised US that serves as the backdrop for the rest of the series, with all the weapons and supercars you’d expect, but the world is more grounded and reactive than before – gone are the days when you could traverse the city like a god. Now, players’ actions have consequences. Walk down the street with a rifle, and the city will have something to say about it. More and more, the games are converging on real life, and non-player characters (NPCs) are acting... well, less like NPCs than ever. For some gamers, there’s a fear that what GTAVI gains in immersion, it loses in the chaos and anarchy that have been part of the series’ DNA since the outset, but for Rockstar, the goal is to create a world of total immersion, which reacts more realistically than ever to what you choose to make of it.

“We look back at our previous games with a critical eye and see where we want to evolve based on what we didn’t do as well as we would have liked to, either because we didn’t have the time, resources or technological capabilities, or in some cases things we just didn’t do as well or consider as fully as we could have,” says Nelson. “A lot of what we do is very iterative – we adjust a lot of things by feel based on what is working and what isn’t.”

en.title: GTA 6 leaks: Rockstar issues statement over online clips
en.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 maker Rockstar Games has issued a statement addressing a series of leaked videos showing the upcoming blockbuster video game.
en.fullContent:
Grand Theft Auto 6 maker Rockstar Games has issued a statement addressing a series of leaked videos showing the upcoming blockbuster video game.

Clips appearing to show gameplay and cinematics from the title began appearing online last week, but the developer did not acknowledge them straight away.

In a statement, the company said the leaks had been "heartbreaking" for the team working on the sequel, and that they were "not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time".

The company apologised for the delays in releasing official updates on the highly anticipated title, but vowed to "exceed" fans' expectations in a special preview airing on Netflix this week.

When leaks first began to surface, there was some doubt as to whether they were genuine.

But as the days went on, evidence mounted to suggest they were legitimate.

en.title: Watch explosive new trailers for Boltgun II and Deathmaster
en.description: Two eagerly anticipated Warhammer video games showed off new trailers in the Future Games Show at Gamescom, and you can watch them both right now.
en.fullContent:
Two eagerly anticipated Warhammer video games showed off new trailers in the Future Games Show at Gamescom, and you can watch them both right now.

The sequel to the adrenaline-pumping throwback shooter Boltgun is already near the top of our wishlist, with its new Battle Sister character, voiced by Alanah Pearce, joining everyone’s favourite Ultramarine lone wolf Malum Caedo for some high speed heretic-slaying. They’ll face their greatest fight yet, as today we learn that Vashtorr the Arkifane is their nemesis.

Such a diabolical villain deserves an entrance like no other, and Vashtorr gets it with his personal music track – Ascent of the Arkifane – composed by FPS soundtrack legend Mick Gordon. The Master of the Soul Forges has unleashed a vast daemonic machine that obliterates an Imperial fleet sent to investigate Chaos activity, and now Caedo and Veyrath must race from planet to planet halting the Daemon’s infernal plans.

Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun II is set to release on 14 October 2026 on PC, PlayStation 5, and XBOX Series X|S, as well as on Nintendo Switch 2 shortly after.

Escape from the depths of the Gnaw and rise through the ranks of the Clans Eshin one stabbed back at a time in Warhammer Age of Sigmar: Deathmaster, with its first ever gameplay trailer released today. Exploit the shadows and strike from the darkness to clear legions of Skaven who stand in your way, earning new abilities and equipment as you claw your way to the top.

All the cunning and conniving in the world won’t save you unless you carve a path to the ranks of the Deathmasters, and in a society as duplicitous as the Skaven, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to put your murderous skills to work. After all, only one in a million Skaven earn true favour from the Great Horned Rat… so make sure it’s you.

en.title: 1047 Games ends active development on Empulse and Splitgate: Arena Reloaded, says it's moving away from live service shooters
en.description: 1047 Games is ending active development on Empulse and Splitgate: Arena Reloaded, moving both titles to peer-to-peer hosting as the studio signals ...
en.fullContent:
1047 Games is ending active development on Empulse and Splitgate: Arena Reloaded, moving both titles to peer-to-peer hosting as the studio signals a broader shift away from live service shooters after ten years.

In a post on X earlier today, the studio said neither game is generating enough revenue to cover the ongoing cost of dedicated servers. It said it had kept covering those costs to give both titles a chance to grow, but had reached a point where doing so was "no longer sustainable."

"We have loved working on these games, playing them, and building them with this community, and we wish we could continue supporting them," the studio said.

From September 3, dedicated servers and matchmaking will shut down for both games, moving them to peer-to-peer hosting with a server browser instead, so players can continue hosting and finding matches. Empulse will get one final new map and a price cut across all regions as part of what the studio called the game's final update.

1047 Games took the same approach with the original Splitgate, which moved to peer-to-peer hosting last year after its dedicated servers went offline, and remains playable today, including on console.

Splitgate 2 released in June 2025 amid a flurry of controversy, which included a MAGA-style "Make FPS Great Again" hat and a $145 cosmetic bundle. Within a month, 1047 Games laid off an undisclosed number of developers, and then a month later, pushed the game "back to beta" and initiated a second wave of layoffs.

en.title: 'Star Wars: Zero Company' review: XCOM-like strategically recaptures the magic of your favorite Star Wars films
en.description: Bitreactor's blend of XCOM combat and a smaller-stakes story nails what makes the Star Wars franchise so special.
en.fullContent:
Bitreactor's blend of XCOM combat and a smaller-stakes story nails what makes the Star Wars franchise so special.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Across the decades, Star Wars' secret sauce has always been a feeling – an intoxicating mixture of whimsy and adventure that’s nearly impossible to replicate. That’s especially true with the original film trilogy and the prequel film trilogy, even if the two have distinctly different flavors.

The series forays into video games have seen a lot of success, but Zero Company does something I’ve never seen a Star Wars game do before: it seamlessly combines the two different eras of the original and prequel film trilogies into something that not only recaptures the magic of those stories, but entirely stands on its own.

By taking the strategic XCOM formula and splicing it together with the whimsy of Star Wars, Zero Company becomes one of the best adventures you can find in a galaxy far, far away.

Command an elite squad through a gritty and authentic Star Wars story set in the twilight of the Clone Wars. Step into the role of Hawks, a former Republic officer leading Zero Company against an emerging threat that could consume the galaxy.
